maria_s: Hi team — Acme ran a scale test and started seeing intermittent 429s around 10:45am PT. They simulated 250 concurrent users and are hitting per-route caps? Need quick triage before EOD.

acme_john: Confirmed — we ramped up with k6 script. First ~30s fine, then a bunch of 429s for the text-generation route. No changes on our side.

alex_se: Can you paste the request headers + response headers from one of the 429s? Also which model + route (e.g., /v1/generate or /v1/chat/completions)?

acme_john: Route: POST /v1/generate -> model: openredwood-1-small. Sample response headers below:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 21 Mar 2026 17:45:12 GMT
x-rw-rate-limit: 180/60
x-rw-burst-remaining: 0
x-rw-token-budget: 110/500
content-type: application/json
```

maria_s: They also saw this after increasing request size (longer prompts) — token usage jumped. They're worried it's a quota thing but the dashboard shows remaining for the account.

jamie_oncall: Quick notes: 1) x-rw-rate-limit looks like a per-route window (180 reqs / 60s). 2) x-rw-burst-remaining==0 means burst exhausted; requests should be queued or get 429s. 3) token-budget header implies token budget is being consumed across concurrent sessions.

priya_se: FYI Acme is on a mid-sized reserved capacity plan — not Dedicated. That means routing falls back to shared capacity if burst exceeds per-route guardrails. Might explain the 429s during a spike.

support_lee: Can you share the k6 script or ramp profile? If they ramped too fast we can suggest a smoothing window.

acme_john: k6 config attached (paste): 
```
scenarios: { ramping: { executor: "ramping-vus", startVUs: 10, stages: [{duration: "30s", target: 250}], gracefulStop: "10s" }}
```

alex_se: That ramp is pretty aggressive for shared routes. Two action items: 1) ask Acme to throttle to 120 concurrent during POC; 2) we can temporarily bump per-route cap for their org for the next hour while they validate. Need ops sign-off.

jamie_oncall: Ops: we can do a temporary per-org per-route uplift + raise burst window. Suggested tweak: per-route window -> 300/60, burst buffer +200 for 1h. Also advise client to enable client-side exponential backoff.

infra-bot: Deploy check: per-route config change for org-acme -> pending approval by eng-ops. CI and safe-guard flags verified.

maria_s: Acme asks about cost impact of raising caps — will they get charged differently?

priya_se: We'll leave pricing unchanged for 1h trial. If they sustain higher usage we'll convert to a short-term add-on (monthly upcharge). I'll coordinate billing.

support_lee: For diagnostics, please also capture one full request/response body (redact PII) and the client-side timeline (timestamps for send/first byte/last byte). That helps root cause if it's client retry storms.

acme_john: Got it. We'll throttle and provide logs. Can you go ahead and request the temporary uplift?

alex_se: Requesting uplift now — tagging eng-ops and jamie_oncall. @jamie_oncall please approve (1h uplift: per-route 300/60, burst +200).

jamie_oncall: Approved, rolling change. I'll monitor metrics for 15m.

infra-bot: Change rolled out for org-acme: per-route limit 300/60, burst buffer 200, expiry 2026-03-21T18:46:20Z.

acme_john: Retesting now — quick update: immediate success, very few 429s, results stabilizing. Thank you.

maria_s: Nicely done. Follow-ups: 1) add recommended client ramp profile to POC playbook; 2) ops to propose a sustained capacity plan if they keep this throughput.

jamie_oncall: Agreed. I'll draft the playbook blurb and dump it in the POC docs. Also we should add an alert rule to detect token-budget drop >30%/5m for mid-tier orgs.

priya_se: I'll coordinate billing options and update the AE with pricing.

maria_s: Closing loop — Acme will run a longer overnight soak at 120 concurrent and share logs in the morning. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
